_comment: Explicit CI shard assignment for the browser suite (4 parallel runners). Every e2e/*.spec.ts must appear in exactly one group (scripts/e2e-shard.mjs enforces this in CI). E10 generated route coverage replaces the old duplicate axe route loops; focused legacy keyboard/menu/theme regressions remain. Generated scans are split across browser-b/c/d from measured runtimes; no fifth runner. 2026-10-06 (PR #266): the generated route scans and the read-only owner/portal section scans run in Playwright parallel mode (both workers), and groups were rebalanced from measured test-seconds after that change (a 158, b 94, c 105, d 133) to roughly 111-126 each. 2026-10-24 (ACC-3): moved revenue-records and website-editor from browser-b to browser-a because browser-b ran 186s against the 180s budget (a 159, b 341, c 299, d 198 test-seconds). 2026-10-25 (MCP-10a): browser-a ran 179s and browser-d 181s against the 180s budget, so feedback.spec.ts (new, ~18 test-seconds) and crm-workspace.spec.ts (~40-55 test-seconds) moved to browser-c, the lightest group (118s). 2026-10-25 (AR-0a): browser-c ran 3.1m against the 180s budget (a 2.7m, b 1.8m, d 2.6m), so crm-workspace.spec.ts (~45-55 test-seconds) moved to browser-b, the lightest group. 2026-10-25 (MCP-1): measured a 2.7m, b 3.1m (over budget once crm-workspace landed), c 2.5m, d 2.4m; system-health.spec.ts (now ~14 test-seconds) moved to browser-d and fleet-report.spec.ts (~16 test-seconds) from browser-b to browser-c. 2026-10-25 (AR-0b): measured a 128s, b 215s, c 183s, d 128s (budget 180s), so crm-workspace.spec.ts (~50 test-seconds) moved from browser-b to browser-a and the three new AR-0b specs (today, customer-record, money-bills; ~30 test-seconds together) went to browser-d. 2026-10-25 (AR-11): measured a 194s (over 180), c 111s; revenue-records (~62 test-seconds) moved a to c without removing tests. 2026-10-25 (AR-11): measured a 188s, b 159s, c 174s, d 173s; moved feedback (~18 test-seconds) from a to b with every test retained. 2026-10-25 (MCP-2 preview-security PR #609 CI): browser-a finished 81 tests but crossed the 180s phase budget; website-editor.spec.ts measured 37 test-seconds and moved from a to d, which completed in 132s, preserving every test and the same phase budget. 2026-10-25 (PR #609 follow-up): the next exact-head run showed browser-d 3.1m (its generated route scan took 201 test-seconds), browser-b 2.0m; move the full website-editor spec from d to b, where measured spare capacity is larger, with no test omitted or budget increased. 2026-10-25 (BA-1 PR #610): browser-b passed all 140 checks in 183.48 seconds but crossed 180-second CI budget; browser-d finished in 122.33 seconds. Move complete feedback.spec.ts (~17 measured test-seconds) from b to d, preserving all tests and budget. 2026-10-25 (BA-1 second measured CI): all four browser groups passed tests, but d finished at 180.56s against 180s; b finished at 125.85s. Move intact feedback (~16.2 test-seconds) and today (~11.1 test-seconds) d→b: expected b ~153s, d ~153s. Complete test coverage is preserved without increasing the budget. 2026-10-25 (BA-1 PR #610 current head): browser-b had a real mobile Today overflow and finished 191.87s. Rebalanced intact today (~8s) b→c, books-closing (~10s) b→d, books-reports (~10s) b→a from measured b=191.87/a=136.27/c=145.78/d=145.2. No tests or budget removed.
